meta.subtitle: Hedges cover 2026 and most of 2027; at a price lifted by a late rally, the Base offers modest upside and the Bear case is deep

analystSentiment.commentary:
Vistra's second quarter read well on the company's own measures and poorly on GAAP. Ongoing Operations Adjusted EBITDA rose by more than 30% year over year and management reaffirmed its 2026 ranges, while net income slipped on hedge marks for positions that settle in later years. The release also reported FERC approval of the pending Cogentrix acquisition and announced Helix Digital Infrastructure alongside KKR, KIA and NVIDIA.

We rate the stock HOLD at $160.50. The scenario commentary explains how much that call depends on the price, and the final recommendation gives the levels and events that would change it.

executiveSummary.companyOverview:
Vistra Corp. operates as an integrated retail electricity and power generation company in the United States, based in Irving, Texas. The company description we draw on, retrieved October 6, 2026, says it serves approximately 5 million customers and has generation capacity of approximately 44,000 megawatts across natural gas, nuclear, coal, solar and battery energy storage facilities. The retail side sells electricity and natural gas to residential, commercial and industrial customers; the generation side also handles wholesale energy sales, commodity risk management and fuel procurement.

FY25 revenue was $17.7B, up 3.0%, and FY25 diluted EPS was $2.18. At $160.50 on October 6, 2026 the market capitalization is about $53.9B. This report covers the 10-Q for the quarter ended June 30, 2026 and the earnings release dated August 7, 2026.

thesis.label: HOLD
thesis.body: The HOLD rests on three dependencies. First, the Base needs FY27 consensus EPS of $10.36 to arrive on the Street's own basis, which the vendor does not state; approximately 94% of expected 2027 generation was hedged as of August 3, 2026, which supports that, but reported GAAP EPS can miss it on hedge marks alone. Second, the Base needs the market to keep paying the current-year multiple it pays at $160.50, which takes the stock to $174.05 a year out. Third, the Bear rests on the lowest Street target, and its depth, not a weak Base, is what keeps reward/risk below our BUY bar.

catalysts: Closing of the Cogentrix Transaction, which received FERC approval in August 2026 and is expected to close in late 2026; the growth section sets out the terms.
Start of deliveries under the Meta nuclear PPAs, which the 10-Q anticipates for a portion of the operating energy and capacity in late 2026.
Formal guidance for 2027, when the company issues it, which would show whether the 2027 midpoint opportunity holds up as a range the company stands behind.
Closing of the sale of the Casco Bay, Beaver Falls and Syracuse gas plants, expected in the second half of 2026, a source of cash the cash-flow discussion weighs.
risks: Leverage could rise again when Cogentrix closes; the balance-sheet discussion sets out where debt stood at FY25 and what has changed since.
Nuclear PTC revenue already recorded for 2024 and 2025 could change if Treasury guidance on gross receipts differs from the company's interpretation.
If electricity demand does not grow at the rate expected, the multiple has room to fall well below today's, which is the Bear case.

income.note: Source: Bigdata.com company tearsheet (FMP); fiscal years ended December 31.

financials.incomeCommentary:
FY25 revenue rose 3.0% to $17.7B, but operating margin fell to 10.7% from 23.7% in FY24 and diluted EPS dropped to $2.18 from $7.00. The proxy statement dated March 18, 2026 says FY25 net income of $944 million included an unrealized loss from hedges expected to settle in future years of $808 million, so FY25 EPS is not the earnings base.

The second quarter repeated the pattern. Revenue fell 5.5% year over year to $4B and operating margin was 13.8%. Net income was $305 million, compared with $327 million a year earlier; the release attributes the {- $22 million -} decrease "primarily" to an increase in unrealized mark-to-market losses of $488 million on derivative positions, "mostly offset" by higher realized prices and capacity revenue and three months' contribution from the plants acquired from Lotus. Ongoing Operations Adjusted EBITDA rose {+ $418 million +} to $1,767 million, which the release attributes primarily to higher realized energy and capacity prices and the Lotus plants. For the six months ended June 30, 2026, net income was $1,334 million compared with $59 million a year earlier.

Adjusted EBITDA is non-GAAP: the release defines it as "EBITDA as adjusted for unrealized gains or losses from hedging activities" and other listed items, and the Ongoing Operations version excludes the Asset Closure segment. The marks it removes belong to positions that settle in later years, so they are not noise. The business is earning more than the FY25 GAAP line shows, as the trailing operating margin of 18.5% and net margin of 11.6% suggest, but the reported line will stay volatile.

The vendor's FY26 revenue estimate of $22.5B carries a +27% growth figure, while second-quarter revenue fell. No source we hold explains that gap and the estimate's basis is not stated, so we give it no weight; the scenarios rest on consensus EPS, and the valuation section explains why that figure can be used.

balance.note: Source: Bigdata.com company tearsheet (FMP); fiscal years ended December 31.

financials.balanceCommentary:
Total debt rose every year through FY25, to $18.8B. Net debt was $18.1B at FY25, up from $10.9B at FY23, and total equity was $5.1B. The current ratio was 0.78 at FY25 and 0.97 on a trailing basis, so current liabilities exceed current assets on both measures.

Leverage on the latest figures may have eased. The trailing net debt/EBITDA of 3.5x sits below the ratio that FY25 net debt and FY25 EBITDA give, and Vistra Operations repaid $2.444 billion of Term Loan B-3 borrowings in April 2026, after FY25. Trailing interest coverage is 3.1x.

The credit profile also improved. S&P raised Vistra Operations' issuer credit rating to BBB- on December 2, 2025 and its Senior Unsecured Notes rating on March 20, 2026, and Fitch moved both ratings to BBB- on March 16, 2026. After those upgrades, and with other conditions in the indenture satisfied, the collateral securing the Senior Secured Notes was released on April 2, 2026; the 10-Q says the release did not change their principal, maturity or interest rates. At June 30, 2026, total available liquidity was approximately $6,295 million, including cash and cash equivalents of $435 million. In June 2026 Permian Power entered a $583 million loan agreement with the Texas Energy Fund, non-recourse to Vistra, with $172 million outstanding at June 30, 2026.

The excerpts we hold give no total debt for June 30, 2026. The balance sheet looks adequate for the current plan with little slack, given the current ratio above. We expect debt to rise again when the Cogentrix cash and assumed debt arrive at closing; the cash-flow discussion weighs how much of the remaining spending needs debt.

cashflow.note: Source: Bigdata.com company tearsheet (FMP); fiscal years ended December 31.

financials.cashflowCommentary:
Operating cash flow was $4.1B in FY25, below $5.5B in FY23 and $4.6B in FY24, while capital expenditure grew every year to $2.8B. The vendor's free cash flow therefore fell to $1.3B, a 7.4% margin, from $3.8B in FY23. In FY25, share repurchases of $1.0B and dividends of $0.3B together used roughly all of it. The trailing FCF yield is 4.2%.

The company manages to Adjusted Free Cash Flow before Growth, which the release defines as cash from operating activities excluding changes in margin deposits and working capital and "adjusted for maintenance capital expenditures, other net investment activities, and other items", so it deducts maintenance rather than all capital spending. On August 7, 2026 the company reaffirmed 2026 Ongoing Operations Adjusted FCFbG guidance of $3.925 billion to $4.725 billion. The two measures are not comparable; we use the vendor's for the history and the company's as its own view of cash before growth.

The near-term growth bill is smaller than a list of projects suggests. The 10-Q projects less than 20% of the Meta uprate spend by year end 2028, the Permian peakers carry their own non-recourse TxEF loan, part of the Cogentrix price is paid in Vistra shares, and the pending plant sale should bring in proceeds. That leaves the Cogentrix cash and the Helix commitment as the main items that may need debt, so on this reading the balance sheet is a constraint to manage rather than the deciding issue for the call, which turns on demand and the multiple, as the Bear case sets out.

multiples.note: Peer multiples pending a peer data source.

valuation.multiplesCommentary:
At $160.50 the stock trades at 27.1x trailing-twelve-month earnings, 16.8x on the vendor's NTM line and about 15.5x FY27 consensus EPS of $10.36. That NTM figure lines up with FY26 consensus EPS of $9.58 rather than a blended next-twelve-month figure, so it is in effect a current-year multiple.

The trailing multiple appears to rest on reported earnings, which carry unrealized hedge marks: it is far lower than FY25 diluted EPS alone would produce, which fits the much stronger first-half 2026 net income shown in the financials section. The vendor does not say whether consensus EPS is GAAP or adjusted. We still use it, because the forward multiples on the page divide today's price by these same consensus lines, so the Base multiple and the EPS it is applied to share one basis, whatever that basis is. Because the trailing multiple may sit on a different basis, we do not read the step down from it to the forward multiples as earnings growth alone.

EV/EBITDA is 13.5x on the vendor's trailing EBITDA. That EBITDA is not the company's measure: the vendor shows FY25 EBITDA of $3.9B, while the proxy reports 2025 Ongoing Operations Adjusted EBITDA of $5,912 million, and we use the vendor's figure for the multiple without restating it on the company's basis.

The data we hold carries no peer multiples, so we make no relative-value claim. We anchor Base to price-to-earnings on consensus EPS, and Bull and Bear to Street targets.

scenarios.name: Bull
scenarios.driver: Price at the Street consensus target of $210.25. Cogentrix closes in late 2026 as expected, Meta deliveries begin as the 10-Q anticipates, and 2027 Ongoing Operations Adjusted EBITDA reaches the top half of the company's $7.4 billion to $7.8 billion midpoint opportunity. The market then pays the Street's price for FY27 consensus EPS, a higher multiple than it pays today.

scenarios.name: Base
scenarios.driver: 16.8x, the multiple the market pays on FY26 consensus EPS at today's price, applied to FY27 consensus EPS of $10.36. The company lands inside its 2026 guidance, the mostly hedged 2027 delivers consensus on the Street's basis, and one year from now the stock carries the same current-year multiple on 2027 earnings. Because the multiple is taken at today's price, this Base inherited the late rally. No re-rating and no contribution beyond consensus.

scenarios.name: Bear
scenarios.driver: Price at the lowest Street target, $106.00. Electricity demand does not grow at the rate expected or new supply lowers wholesale prices, both 10-K risk factors; Cogentrix or the Meta deliveries slip, 2027 EPS holds near the FY26 consensus of $9.58, and the market stops paying for growth beyond the hedged years. At that price the stock would trade well below the Base case's current-year multiple even on the lower EPS, so most of the fall comes from the multiple.

valuation.scenarioCommentary:
The Street is close to unanimous: 20 of 21 analysts rate the stock Buy and one rates it Sell, with targets from $106.00 to $305.00 around a consensus of $210.25 and a median of $211.00.

The price history on the page shows a 52-week range of $132.66 to $217.10 and, more recently, a sharp rise in the two sessions up to October 6, 2026, most of it in the latest one, from lower levels where the stock had traded for weeks. No source we hold explains either move. Read against the published scenario prices, most of those earlier closes derive BUY and today's price derives HOLD, so the call rests on the current price. The Base, as its driver notes, inherited the rise; at the earlier prices the same method would have given a lower Base, so the BUY those closes show on the published prices overstates what a report written then would have said. We keep the anchor because it ties the Base to a multiple and an EPS a reader can check, rather than to a target, but the Base carries a move we cannot explain.

We put 55% on Base because the year it depends on is mostly hedged, as the growth section sets out, and the company reaffirmed its 2026 ranges in August. Bull gets 25%: the stock traded above the Bull price within the past year and the Street consensus sits there, but the 2027 figure Bull leans on is a midpoint opportunity that the release says is not guidance.

Bear gets 20%, argued on its own terms. The hedges protect most of 2027, so within a year the Bear runs mainly through the multiple. What supports it is the width of the past year's price range, the thinner hedge cover for 2028 and the Cogentrix cash still to be paid. What keeps it below Bull is that the Bear price sits below anything the stock has traded at in the past 52 weeks.

These weights derive HOLD, with the figures in the final recommendation. Swapping the Bull and Bear weights still derives HOLD, and SELL needs a Bear weight far above Bull's or a Base well below the price. BUY at today's price needs two changes together: with the Bear at the 52-week low and five points moved from Bear to Bull, the same math derives BUY. We do not use that Bear, because a return to a recent low is a move inside the past year's range, not a case with lower earnings. The call is close on price and less close on the scenarios.

segments.name: Consolidated
segments.body: The vendor's segment line carries only a consolidated FY25 total of $17.7B. The company's own release shows more: it reports Adjusted EBITDA for Retail, Texas, East, West, Corporate and Other, and Asset Closure, and the company description lists five segments. We follow the company. In the second quarter, compared with the same quarter of 2025, Adjusted EBITDA rose to $311 million from $142 million in Texas, to $642 million from $418 million in East and to $68 million from $49 million in West, while Retail was $773 million compared with $756 million. For the six months, Retail fell to $841 million from $940 million, so its decline came earlier in the year. The release explains the consolidated change, not each segment's. The regional segments carried the year-over-year growth; Retail is the open question, and we would want its second-half figures before calling a trend.

moatFactors.name: Integrated retail and generation
moatFactors.body: The 10-Q says Vistra's "integrated retail electricity and power generation operations allow us to quickly respond to electricity demand changes." We treat owning both the customers and the plants as a partial natural hedge. The 10-K gives the counter-case: retail faces "significant competition from other REPs", and "volatile power supply costs and demand for power have and could in the future adversely affect" retail results. Integration is a real but partial advantage.

moatFactors.name: Long-dated nuclear contracts
moatFactors.body: The 20-year nuclear agreements with Meta and AWS described under growth turn part of the nuclear fleet's output into contracted revenue, and the NRC approved the license renewal for Perry in July 2025, extending it through 2046. Contracts of this length are hard to win without licensed plants already running, in our judgment. The limits are timing and the uprate approvals covered under risks; the AWS deliveries are anticipated to reach full capacity only by 2032.

moatFactors.name: Hedging program
moatFactors.body: The release says the company's "comprehensive hedging program provides support for" its 2026 ranges and its 2027 midpoint opportunity. The hedge book is the main source of Vistra's near-term earnings visibility. The 10-K sets the limit: its assets or positions "cannot be fully hedged", and "hedging transactions may not work as planned or hedge counterparties may default on their obligations." The marks on those hedges also run through GAAP earnings, as the financials section shows.

businessMoat.durability: We rate the moat NARROW. Contracts, integration and hedging give Vistra some insulation. The contracted nuclear output covers part of the fleet; the rest of the fleet and the retail book remain exposed to the wholesale price swings described under systemic risks. The 10-K also warns that market participants may keep building or expanding generation "despite relatively low power prices", which could reduce wholesale prices. The nuclear PTC, available to existing nuclear facilities from 2024 through 2032, is support with an end date. The advantages last as long as the contracts and licenses do, but the commodity exposure stays.

points: On August 7, 2026 Vistra reaffirmed 2026 guidance of $6.8 billion to $7.6 billion for Ongoing Operations Adjusted EBITDA; the proxy reports $5,912 million for 2025. As of August 3, 2026 it had hedged approximately 100% of expected 2026 generation volumes. With the year hedged, we expect 2026 to land inside the range, and the range's width is the main uncertainty.

The release puts the 2027 Ongoing Operations Adjusted EBITDA midpoint opportunity at $7.4 billion to $7.8 billion but says it is "not intended to be guidance" and rests on market curves as of October 31, 2025; it excludes Cogentrix and the Meta PPAs. Hedge cover steps down from approximately 94% of expected 2027 generation to approximately 72% for 2028, so the path after 2027 is more open.

In January 2026 Vistra announced it had entered into 20-year PPAs to supply Meta with a total of 2,609 MW from its PJM nuclear plants, including uprates at Perry, Davis-Besse and Beaver Valley. The 10-Q anticipates full delivery of the operating energy and capacity by year end 2027 and of the uprates by year end 2034. Under a 20-year PPA announced in September 2025, Vistra anticipates power delivery to AWS of 1,200 MW from Comanche Peak to begin in the fourth quarter of 2027. These contracts add more after 2027 than within it.

The pending Cogentrix Transaction adds 10 natural gas generation facilities totaling approximately 5,500 MW. Consideration at closing is approximately $2.3 billion in cash, net of adjustments for the assumption of an estimated $1.5 billion of Cogentrix indebtedness, plus 5,000,000 Vistra shares at a mutually agreed-upon value of $185 per share, above today's price. The 10-K warns that Vistra "may not realize the anticipated synergies." The deal adds debt and shares before it adds earnings.

In July 2026 Vistra cleared 10,924 MW in the PJM capacity auction for planning year 2028-2029 at $325.00 per MW-day in every zone it reported. In Texas, a plan announced in May 2024 includes up to 860 MW of peaking plants, which the 10-Q describes as in early development and anticipates online in 2028, and a repowering of Coleto Creek of up to 600 MW, on which it gives no update. The capacity price supports revenue in years beyond our scenarios.

management.leadership: The proxy statement dated March 18, 2026 lists James A. Burke, President and Chief Executive Officer, and Kristopher E. Moldovan, Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer, among the 2025 named executive officers. Per the proxy, 2025 Ongoing Operations Adjusted EBITDA was $112 million above the guidance midpoint announced in November 2024, and Ongoing Operations Adjusted FCFbG was $292 million above the original guidance midpoint. The August 7, 2026 release says Vistra achieved commercial availability of 97% or greater across its fleet during recent periods of extreme heat in Texas and the PJM market. The counterweight is that these beats are on adjusted measures, while FY25 GAAP net income fell, as the financials section shows. We credit management with execution against its own targets.
management.capitalAllocation:
Buybacks have been the main return of capital. As of August 3, 2026, Vistra had executed $6.5 billion of repurchases since November 2021 and had 336 million shares outstanding, a 30% reduction from November 2, 2021; $1.2 billion of authorization remained, which it expects to complete no later than year-end 2027. The dividend yield is 0.64%.

Vistra acquired the Lotus plants (2,600 MW) on October 22, 2025 for a base purchase price of $1.9 billion, has Cogentrix pending, and is selling its Casco Bay, Beaver Falls and Syracuse plants. In June 2026 it committed up to $1 billion to the Helix Fund, managed by affiliates of KKR: an initial $500 million and $500 million more subject to "certain commercial power supply milestones for our existing generation assets" or, at its election, regardless. The release calls the full amount an initial commitment; we use the 10-Q's split.

Helix is a fund investment, not capital spent on Vistra's own plants, but the company ties it to the fleet: the fund targets assets including "baseload and flexible power generation", and the release cites "Vistra's role as Helix's preferred power provider". The link could turn into power sales from the existing fleet; the risk is that Vistra's capital sits in a fund it does not manage. With the Cogentrix cash still to pay, we would rather see the remaining buyback paced than accelerated.
management.governance: The proxy statement dated March 18, 2026 says the Board determined Mses. Ackermann, Acosta, Crutchfield and Lagacy and Messrs. Baiera, Barbas, Helm, Pitesa, Sult and Walters to be independent. During 2025 the CEO and Chairman roles were separate, though the Board has no policy requiring that. Mrs. Acosta and Messrs. Barbas and Sult qualify as Audit Committee financial experts. The proxy describes a pay philosophy that "places an emphasis on 'pay-at-risk'", and the Annual Incentive Plan weights Adjusted EBITDA, Adjusted FCFbG and other metrics including total cost; the proxy says above-target performance on Adjusted EBITDA and Adjusted FCFbG "contributed to strong incentive plan payouts for 2025." If the plan's Adjusted EBITDA follows the release definition, annual bonuses track a measure that excludes unrealized hedge results. The excerpt does not show the board's full size, long-term awards or beneficial ownership, so we make no claim on the independent share of the board or on insider stakes. On what it shows, the board structure is conventional, and the Audit and compensation committee members it names meet heightened independence standards.

idiosyncratic: Credit reversion. The 10-Q says the collateral release on the Senior Secured Notes "is subject to reversion" if the rating agencies withdraw the investment-grade ratings or downgrade them below investment grade, subject to a 60-day grace period. The June 2026 amendments removed the collateral reinstatement requirements for the credit facilities, so a downgrade would bring back the liens on the notes only. For a holder, the cost would be a weaker credit position just as the Cogentrix cash and assumed debt land, not a return to the pre-2026 structure.

Nuclear PTC estimates. Vistra recognized transferable nuclear PTC revenues of $220 million in 2025 and $545 million in 2024. The 10-Q says Treasury guidance on gross receipts that differs from the company's interpretation "could result in a material change to PTC revenues recorded in 2024 and 2025", booked as a change in estimate when received. The size of any change is unknown.

Offtake and uprate execution. The 10-K lists the risk that "electricity demand does not grow at the rate expected" or that Vistra cannot execute on large load offtake opportunities, including agreements already signed. For the Meta uprates, the 10-Q says the timing and amount of spending will depend on "regulatory approvals, engineering evaluations and capital allocation decisions". The operating-plant deliveries carry less of that risk; the uprates sit years out, and we see the most room for slippage there.

Cogentrix completion. The 10-K (February 27, 2026) says Vistra "may not be able to consummate the Cogentrix Transactions on the anticipated terms, on the anticipated timeline, or at all." The 10-Q lists the expiration or termination of Hart-Scott-Rodino waiting periods among the closing conditions, and the excerpt does not say that has happened. A failed deal would take part of the Bull case away, but it would also leave the cash consideration unspent, so we do not add it to the Bear.
risks.systemic: Wholesale power prices drive revenue: the 10-K says Vistra's "revenues, results of operations, and operating cash flows are affected by price fluctuations in the wholesale power market and other market factors beyond our control", and lists fuel costs next. The 10-Q adds the conflict involving the United States, Israel and Iran: Vistra does not operate in the region, but prolonged instability "could indirectly affect the Company" through natural gas and power prices, supply chains, construction delays, inflation and capital-market volatility. Supply chain constraints and labor shortages are already raising equipment and labor costs, per the 10-Q. Regulation is the other broad exposure: the 10-K cites changes to market structure, state or federal interference in power markets, subsidized generation, and laws "proposed or implemented under the Trump administration." It also says extreme weather and seasonality have hurt results before. The hedge book softens price risk for 2026 and 2027 but does not remove these exposures.

body: We rate Vistra HOLD with a target range of $148–$178. The weighted fair value of $169.49 gives expected upside of +5.6%, the Bear case sits 34.0% below the price, and reward/risk is 0.16×. We set the range where the published scenarios change the label: below the low end they derive BUY, and above the high end they derive SELL. For a holder, today's price sits inside the range and the scenarios give no reason to sell. For a buyer, the latest rally is a reason to wait for the low end rather than pay today's price.

Away from price, a label change needs the scenarios to move as far as the scenario commentary shows. We would move to BUY if 2027 guidance, when issued, sits at or above the top of the midpoint-opportunity range with Cogentrix closed, because that would lift the earnings floor enough to raise the Bear toward the 52-week low and shift weight from Bear to Bull. We would move to SELL if 2027 guidance comes in far enough below that range to pull the Base well below the price. A downgrade of Vistra Operations below investment grade would add weight to the Bear but would not on its own derive SELL.
